title: Coordinated control of both microtubule ends regulates mitotic spindle length
task: Resolve spindle length control via coordinated regulation of microtubule ends
key_results: Mathematical model demonstrates length-dependent regulation at both MT ends enables independent variation of spindle length and poleward flux velocity; protein depletion experiments confirm dual-end perturbations can decouple these parameters; evidence for length-dependent protein accumulation at minus-ends
comments: The model elegantly resolves a long-standing contradiction in spindle biophysics, though direct measurement of protein dynamics at minus-ends during live mitosis would further validate the mechanism.

model_io.model: Mathematical model of poleward flux and length-dependent dynamics
Protein depletion experiments in human cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Length-dependent regulation at both MT ends allows independent control of spindle length and poleward flux
hypotheses.result: Model predicts and experiments confirm spindle length and flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous dual-end perturbations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Proteins accumulate at MT minus-ends in a length-dependent manner
hypotheses.result: Experimental evidence for length-dependent protein accumulation at spindle pole minus-ends

title: Molecular basis of PADI6 species-specific oligomerization in maternal regulatory complexes
task: Characterize species-specific PADI6 oligomerization in maternal complexes
key_results: Mouse PADI6 forms tetramers and higher-order filamentous assemblies via N-terminal IgG domain, whereas human PADI6 shows reduced oligomerization; distinct oligomeric states alter MPU stoichiometry between species
comments: Cryo-EM structural data for mPADI6 oligomers would strengthen the mechanistic understanding, though the species-specific differences are significant for embryonic development models.

model_io.model: MPU complex reconstitution + cryo-EM analysis
outputs: cryo-EM structure of mPADI6 N-terminal IgG-mediated assemblies
stoichiometric ratios in mMPU and hMPU

hypotheses.hypothesis: N-terminal IgG domain mediates species-specific PADI6 oligomerization
hypotheses.result: mPADI6 N-terminal IgG domain drives tetramer and filament formation; human PADI6 with same domain shows reduced oligomerization in solution

title: De novo design of protein binders targeting the human sweet taste receptor as potential sweet proteins
task: Design protein binders for sweet taste receptor TAS1R2
key_results: Designed three distinct TAS1R2-binding proteins with varying structural stability and interaction profiles; Binder1 formed largest interface with most favorable GBSA energy; Binder2 showed strongest Boltz-1 confidence

title: Identification of a natural product inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro through integrated virtual screening, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations
task: Identify SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors via integrated virtual screening and molecular dynamics
key_results: Lig14 identified from 224,205 natural products with binding energy −8.2 kcal/mol (superior to Paxlovid −7.6 kcal/mol), MM-GBSA free energy −31.82 ± 6.64 kcal/mol, sustained binding with sub-diffusive motion (α=0.49) and 35.2 Å confinement; C145Y and π-sulfur bonding predicted to disrupt catalytic dyad
comments: Comprehensive in silico pipeline is rigorous but lacks experimental validation; predicted catalytic mechanism disruption through non-standard interactions (π-sulfur) requires biochemical confirmation.

model_io.model: Virtual screening pipeline: ZINC15 database → docking → DFT → MD simulations
Alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP)
outputs: Solvation free energy ΔGsolv across four methods

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lig14 binds Mpro with higher affinity than Paxlovid
hypotheses.result: Docking binding energy −8.2 kcal/mol vs Paxlovid −7.6 kcal/mol; MM-GBSA free energy −31.82 ± 6.64 kcal/mol supports competitive inhibition

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lig14 maintains persistent binding through sub-diffusive motion and active site confinement
hypotheses.result: MD simulations show α=0.49 sub-diffusive motion with 35.2 Å confinement and ~360 Å² contact area

hypotheses.hypothesis: C145Y and π-sulfur interactions with catalytic residues disrupt Mpro activity
hypotheses.result: Predicted disruption of H41-C145 catalytic dyad formation via novel bonding modes in mutant variants (G143S/D/N, E166K)

title: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function
task: Establish microglial role in fragile X syndrome pathogenesis through FMRP-regulated lysosomal function and progranulin signaling
key_results: Selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia recapitulates FXS phenotypes (audiogenic seizures and parvalbumin neuron loss); FMRP binds lysosomal mRNAs and promotes lysosomal protein expression; FMRP deficiency reduces progranulin expression increasing PV neuron apoptosis; progranulin overexpression rescues AGS and PV neuron loss in Fmr1−/y mice
comments: Novel identification of microglial FMRP and progranulin as FXS drivers suggests therapeutic targeting may bypass neuronal resistance to previous interventions.

model_io.model: Mice with selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia
Microglia with Fmr1 deletion
Fmr1−/y and Grn+/− mice with combination studies

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microglial FMRP regulates lysosomal function and progranulin secretion; deficiency reduces progranulin-mediated PV neuron survival driving FXS pathology
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; selective microglial Fmr1 deletion recapitulates FXS phenotypes; progranulin overexpression rescues pathology

title: Phosphorylation of IRS4 at YY111/112 promotes LUSC progression via PI3K/AKT pathway activation

comments: Identifies therapeutically tractable Src-IRS4-PI3K/AKT axis in LUSC; phosphopeptide approach offers innovative targeting strategy for blocking Src-driven IRS4 activation.

title: SIL1 modulates Reelin signaling during cortical neuron migration

comments: Study mechanistically links endoplasmic reticulum quality control to Reelin pathway regulation; however, whether SIL1 directly or indirectly stabilizes these Reelin components remains unclear.

model_io.model: Analysis of single-cell sequencing databases of human cortical development

key_results: CDK4/6i predominantly activates PERK; PERK inhibition combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR signaling and accelerates senescence commitment with RB dephosphorylation; CDK4/6i+ISRIB combination reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents via enhanced senescence and immune surveillance
comments: Identification of PERK as critical mediator of CDK4/6i response provides rationale for combination therapy; mechanistic link to immune activation offers broader therapeutic implications.

AnkB-deficient male mice on high-fat diet

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen identifies mutation-specific pathways converging on TAZ/TEAD activation in mutant p53-driven breast cancer
